chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Asbaat, from Yaqoub bin Salim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Free the way of the insolvent just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, frees it.

key_terms.الْمُعْسِرِ: The insolvent debtor who has the means to pay but is currently constrained or delayed.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling regarding debtors who are insolvent?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the legal ruling of granting respite to the insolvent debtor (*mu'sir*) with the divine attribute of Allah’s leniency, establishing a spiritual dimension to financial jurisprudence. This narration is foundational in Shia fiqh for prioritizing mercy over strict contractual enforcement, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of 'freeing' the debtor as an act of worship. It underscores the principle that just as Allah relieves His creation from spiritual and worldly burdens, creditors should emulate this divine grace in their dealings.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Yaqoub Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>: ‘
Free the way of the insolvent just as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Frees it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Ya’qub ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that you must leave alone a borrower who has difficulty repaying a loan, just as Allah does (extend the due time for payment of loan if the borrower has difficulty repaying. . . ” (see [2:280]).
